refuted.departure: The scheme token is matched ignoring case (RFC 7235 says auth-scheme is case-insensitive, so this is a natural reading). `gw-hmac-sha256 keyId=...` verifies instead of being malformed-authorization. No graded set, mutant or probe carries a scheme token in any case other than the exact one.

The parameter names keyId and signature are matched ignoring case (auth-param names are case-insensitive in RFC 7235). `keyid=gw-prod-01, Signature=<good>` verifies instead of malformed-authorization. Nothing graded varies the case of a parameter name.

The keyId value inside the header is compared to the record's key id ignoring case, so `keyId=GW-PROD-01` on a gw-prod-01 record verifies. hard h1 seq 7 tests case on the x-gw-key-id header (unknown-key-id), and h3 seq 2 tests a different key id, but nothing tests a same-key-different-case keyId inside the Authorization value. Not the key-id-any-case mutant (that lowercases the record key id, caught by hard h1 seq 7).

After the comma, any run of one or more spaces/tabs is accepted (regex `,[ \t]+signature=`). Zero spaces is still malformed, so h3 seq 4 (`,signature=`) still passes, and the auth-loose-separator mutant is different (it accepts zero spaces). Two spaces after the comma verifies instead of malformed-authorization.

Optional spaces/tabs are tolerated around each `=` and before the comma (regex `keyId[ \t]*=[ \t]*<id>[ \t]*, signature[ \t]*=`), with the single space after the scheme and the `, ` separator kept exact. `keyId = gw-prod-01 , signature = <good>` verifies instead of malformed-authorization. Nothing graded puts whitespace at those positions.

After the scheme token any run of one or more spaces is accepted (regex `GW-HMAC-SHA256 +keyId=`). Base variant: survives all 4 sets. Hard variant: caught by hard/h2 seq 5 (`GW-HMAC-SHA256  keyId=gw-prod-01, signature=000...`, expected malformed-authorization, departure gives signature-mismatch). So this is under-graded in base only; h3 is shared, so adding the record to h3 would close it for base.

Auth-param style parsing: the presented signature is the token up to the first comma or whitespace, so trailing parameters or text are ignored. `signature=<good>, nonce=17` verifies instead of signature-mismatch. Not the short-signature-malformed mutant (which rejects non-64-hex and is caught by h2 deadbeef); this departure passes deadbeef, uppercase and padded records exactly as the oracle does.
An RFC 7235 quoted-string value is unquoted before comparison: `signature="<good>"` verifies instead of signature-mismatch. Nothing graded carries a quoted value.

An empty presented signature (nothing after `signature=`) is reported as malformed-authorization instead of signature-mismatch (the sentence says a short signature is a mismatch; empty is the limiting case and the oracle says mismatch). The shortest graded presented signature is `deadbeef` (h2), so the empty case is never graded. Signature field stays filled in both readings.

The strict inverse of AUTH-07: a presented signature containing internal whitespace or a comma (trailing text after the token) is reported as malformed-authorization instead of signature-mismatch. Survives because no graded presented signature has anything after the token.

Input class: an Authorization value with leading (or trailing) whitespace around the whole value, e.g. ` GW-HMAC-SHA256 keyId=...`. Reading 1 (the oracle, scheme.mjs headerOf and solution pipeline.ts headerValue): the header value is trimmed before the prefix check, so it verifies. Reading 2 (the literal sentence): the value does not start with exactly the prefix, so it is malformed-authorization. Both readings reproduce all 8 graded sets. Note the oracle is the one departing from the literal text here.

Input class: the Authorization header NAME in a different case (`authorization`, `AUTHORIZATION`). Every graded Authorization header is spelled exactly `Authorization`, while x-gw-key-id and host appear in several cases. Reading 1 (oracle): name matched case-insensitively, record verified. Reading 2: only a header literally named `Authorization` counts, so the record is signed (and under the signed_headers rule the lowercase `authorization` is excluded from the canonical either way, so canonical_sha256 and signature agree, only outcome differs). The dossier register (01-decision-register.md line 92) states name case-insensitivity for x-gw-key-id only; nothing states it for Authorization.

Input class: two Authorization headers on one record. No graded record has more than one. Reading 1 (oracle, Array.find): the first is verified. Reading 2: the last wins (the example then gives malformed-authorization from `Bearer x`). Reading 3: duplicates are themselves malformed-authorization. All three reproduce all 8 graded sets (readings 2 and 3 both run in the script).

Input class: an Authorization header present with an empty or whitespace-only value. Reading 1 (oracle): the header is carried, so verify, prefix fails, malformed-authorization. Reading 2: an empty header is treated as absent, record is signed. Both reproduce all 8 graded sets.

Input class: a presented signature padded with something other than ASCII space (tab, CR/LF, NBSP U+00A0). h3 seq 1 pads with plain spaces only. Reading 1 (oracle, String.prototype.trim): all Unicode whitespace stripped, verified. Reading 2: only spaces and tabs are 'whitespace' (e.g. the folding regex /[ \t]/ the canonical rule already uses), so NBSP or CRLF padding is a signature-mismatch. Both reproduce all 8 graded sets. Example value is `signature= <good> `.

Input class: an x-gw-key-id value with surrounding whitespace (` gw-prod-01 `). This decides the keyId binding, since the prefix is built from the record key id. Reading 1 (oracle headerOf/headerValue): the value is trimmed, key_id is `gw-prod-01`, the header's `keyId=gw-prod-01` binds, verified. Reading 2: used verbatim, key_id carries the spaces, unknown-key-id with empty signature. The dossier register (01-decision-register.md line 92, 'the value itself is used verbatim') supports reading 2, so the oracle departs from the dossier here as well; instruction.md is silent. No graded key id has surrounding whitespace. Borderline with the keys lens, reported because it changes the keyId binding.

JSON key order. instruction.md says 'Every evidence object has exactly these keys' and lists them, but never states that the keys must be serialised in that order; an agent that emits `reason` right after `outcome` (a natural grouping) produces the same key set, passes test_evidence_is_valid_ndjson, and fails every byte comparison: base sample seq 4,5,7,8; h1 seq 3; h2 seq 2,3; h3 seq 2,3,4,5,6 (hard likewise plus h1 seq 7, h2 seq 5). The starter /app/src/pipeline.ts emits only seq,key_id,method,outcome,signature, so it does not fix the order of the keys the agent must add. Borderline: the list order is a strong implicit cue, so severity low.

The x-gw-key-id header VALUE is used verbatim (as dossier GW-034 states: "the value itself is used verbatim", and the 2025-11-25 note: "The key id value is used exactly as sent") instead of trimmed. The reference (analysis/scheme.mjs headerOf and solution/src/pipeline.ts headerValue) both call .trim() on it, so the oracle contradicts the dossier the agent is told to follow. instruction.md is silent; no graded record has a padded key id, so trimming, not trimming, or trimming only spaces all pass. Note the instruction's only whitespace rule ("compared as is apart from surrounding whitespace") is about the presented signature, not the key id.

When the record carries two x-gw-key-id headers the reference takes the first (Array.find). An agent that builds a header map (Object.fromEntries / new Map over lowercased names), which is the most common JS idiom, takes the last. instruction.md and both dossiers say nothing about repeated headers, and no graded record has one. Both headers still appear in the canonical string either way, so canonical_sha256 agrees and only key_id/signature/outcome differ.

Key lookup that builds the file path first and checks the roster on the resolved file: path.resolve("/app/keys", `${keyId}.key`), then accept if the resolved file's basename is gw-prod-01.key or gw-prod-02.key. The reference checks the id string against the roster before touching the filesystem. The two agree on every graded record (every key id there is a plain id), but a key id of "../keys/gw-prod-01", "./gw-prod-02" or "/app/keys/gw-prod-01" is signed by the departure and unknown-key-id in the reference. Dossier GW-038 ("A key id that does not resolve to an approved key file is a hard rejection") literally describes resolving to a file, so the departure is a natural reading of the material the agent is given. Hard variant sentence: "A request naming a key that isn't on the roster is an `unknown-key-id`, never signed."

The keyId inside the Authorization header is compared to the record's key id without regard to case (prefix parsed with a regex, m[1].toLowerCase() === keyId.toLowerCase()). The record's own key id is still matched exactly against the roster, so the hard h1 uppercase record and the h3 other-key record both still produce the approved bytes. Distinct from ci mutant auth-key-id-unbound (which accepts ANY keyId and is caught by h3 record 2) and from key-id-any-case (which lowercases the record's key id and is caught by hard h1).

Roster key id matched in any case (keyId.toLowerCase() before the roster lookup). This is ci mutant key-id-any-case, which ci/mutate.mjs lists among the hard-variant mutants; reporting it only because the BASE verifier does not catch it: no base graded record carries an upper/mixed-case key id (hard h1 record 7 GW-PROD-01 is the only one, and h1 differs between variants). Base dossier GW-034 says the value is used verbatim, so the correct base behaviour is unknown-key-id. Drop this finding if the base variant is deliberately not graded on it.

An x-gw-key-id header that is present with an empty (or, after trimming, whitespace-only) value. Reference: keyId === "" so missing-key-id. Alternative reading: the header exists, so a key id was given and it is simply not on the roster, unknown-key-id. instruction.md defines key_id as "" "when there isn't one" without saying whether an empty value counts as not having one; no graded record has an empty value. Combined with the verbatim reading (K1) a whitespace-only value even changes the key_id field ("   ").

The verifier requires the key id header NAME to be matched without regard to case: the sample itself mixes "X-GW-Key-Id" (records 1,3,6,7,8) and "x-gw-key-id" (records 2,4), and h1 mixes them too. instruction.md states neither which header carries the key id nor that its name is case-insensitive. Stated in the dossier only: base and hard 01-decision-register.md GW-034 "The key id travels in the `x-gw-key-id` request header. Its value is matched case-insensitively on the header NAME". An agent matching the exact spelling "X-GW-Key-Id" fails sample and h1 in both variants (records 2 and 4 become missing-key-id); matching exactly "x-gw-key-id" fails all 8 sets. Low severity because the sample makes the mixed spelling obvious and HTTP header names are case-insensitive by RFC, but strictly it is graded behaviour the instruction does not state.

How the trailing newline of a key file is removed. Readers that all pass: strip every trailing CR/LF byte (reference), strip exactly one trailing LF, String.prototype.trimEnd on the decoded text, String.prototype.trim. They agree because the 6 shipped key files are all exactly 32 bytes + one LF. On other file shapes they diverge: CRLF -> strip-one-lf keeps 33 bytes while the others keep 32; two LFs -> strip-one-lf keeps 33; a leading space -> only trim drops it (32 vs 33). Only the verbatim reader (33 bytes, ci mutant key-file-verbatim) is caught. Not exercisable by any request record; it would take a differently-terminated roster key file in the environment, which the verifier never introduces.

A roster id (gw-prod-01/02) whose file is missing or unreadable. Reference solution/src/pipeline.ts catches the readFileSync error and reports unknown-key-id with signature "" and canonical_sha256 still filled; analysis/scheme.mjs likewise (keyFiles.has(id) false -> unknown-key-id). A plausible alternative is to let the error propagate (non-zero exit, no evidence line), or a distinct reason. instruction.md says nothing, and test_only_approved_key_files_are_opened only makes the OFF-roster key unreadable, so the roster-key failure path is never exercised and every behaviour passes.
